_what: proof (a) scored over the CANONICAL paper-core baseline set, not a set I chose.
_the_set: the ACTIVE (non-#) lines of results/orchestration/live2/frozen_test/runs/BASELINE_MATRIX, 'D164 BASELINE MATRIX ... the paper core, seeds 4-7'. 18 distinct arms, every active line at the single tag _L3_epg_rq30, verified by reading the committed file rather than from a relay.
_scoring_rule_ONE_RECIPE_ONLY: scored against the committed d179 17-arm table ALONE (d208_proof_a_bars.json). An arm absent from d179 may use its own record ONLY if TWO records agree. NEVER a union across records: a union would have taken covex-v6-rules as a3c000f4ae2f37f5 / 12,179 from the single older d175_digest_proofs.json against 18067c4c66bb44b8 / 11,955 in eleven records, scoring a CORRECT cell as MOVED and firing the escalation clause on a sound measurement. d175's value is recorded as SUPERSEDED.
_load_boundary: for --cutoff-off DIGEST cells load is not a comparability threat, because the planner wall-clock cutoff is patched off so the time-dependent quantity is out of play; for anything TIMING-dependent it is. This rests on TWO legs, the MECHANISM and TODAY'S OWN bit-exact matches at loadavg 10.80 and 13.80, and NOT on precedent: the highest load any committed artefact records is 9.00 (d184_r3_c5attr_proofs.json), d179 carries only a boolean with no magnitude, and the earlier 'precedent at about 20' claim was checked and withdrawn.
_no_new_cells_were_needed: every matrix arm that HAS a d179 bar is already in the running chain, so the 18-arm table needs no GPU beyond it. The 13 no-bar arms and the three hit-6 readers (preble, b9, uniscale) are NOT in the active matrix at all, so no before-digest is owed for them.

b7-edf-feasibility._STRONGEST_LOAD_DATA_POINT: bit-exact against an independently committed bar at loadavg 20.45, which is MORE THAN TWICE the highest load any committed artefact records (9.00, d184_r3_c5attr_proofs.json). This is now the load boundary's best empirical leg, and it comes from the regime actually in use rather than from a precedent.
